dedupe_keys.name: highway pv capacity potential on 3 000 km of italian highways a gis driven assessment

description: This study by Alessandro Niccolai, Vincenzo Cirimele, Diego Franceschini, Valerio Apicella, Benedetto Carambia and Sonia Leva of the Politecnico di Milano and the University of Bologna, published in Sustainable Energy Technologies and Assessments in 2025, presents a method to assess automatically the photovoltaic potential of areas near highways from GIS data, motivated by electricity demand from electric mobility. Coverage: about 3,000 km of Italian highways; the assessment considers different installation options, the morphology of each area and installation and maintenance costs. It finds that 85% of the available areas could be used, for an estimated 926 MWp of capacity and 830 GWh of production a year. Format and access: an open journal article. Licence and cost: free under CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Caveats: the abstract was the part read; the highway operator and data sources are not named in it. The per-area capacities can set roadside generation for charging and road energy supply in capacity planning models. It relates to the JRC European road and rail PV study and The Ray ROW Solar mapping tool in the catalogue.
